Configures the background directory sync.

| Key | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`ldap.sync.interval`](#interval) | duration | `15m` |
| [`ldap.sync.disable_after`](#disable_after) | int | `3` |
| [`ldap.sync.reenable`](#reenable) | bool | `true` |
| [`ldap.sync.extra_groups`](#extra_groups) | list | `empty` |

## `interval`

`duration`, default `15m`

How often the sync runs. Zero disables the job entirely.

```yaml
ldap:
  sync:
    interval: 15m
```

## `disable_after`

`int`, default `3`

How many consecutive *successful* searches that find no entry it takes before the user is auto-disabled. A directory outage is never a miss: only a search that succeeds and finds nothing counts.

```yaml
ldap:
  sync:
    disable_after: 3
```

## `reenable`

`bool`, default `true`

Lets the sync clear its own disables when a directory entry reappears. It only ever clears disables whose source is exactly ldap_sync; a user disabled by an admin or SOC operator is never touched by the sync, in either direction.

```yaml
ldap:
  sync:
    reenable: true
```

## `extra_groups`

`list`, default `empty`

Group names to persist in addition to those the rest of the configuration references — a future notification target, say. See the allowlist rule on user_groups.
